title: CD-SEM Measurement - Residue Detection on Zeta-388
subtitle: Post-CMP Quality Validation for 45nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Klaus Weber

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Zeta-388 system to detect and classify Residue defects during post-cmp inspection at the 45nm technology node. The test is conducted at Chandler Fab 42 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Residue defects that are critical to yield at the 45nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Zeta-388 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Zeta-388
- Inspection Type: CD-SEM Measurement
- Target Defect: Residue
- Process Step: Post-CMP
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 45nm
- Fab Location: Chandler Fab 42

This test case applies to all Zeta-388 systems deployed at Chandler Fab 42 for post-cmp monitoring in the 45nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Zeta-388
Software Version: v14.2.343
Recipe: CD-SEM_MEASUREMENT_45nm_POST_CMP
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Low (72 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 1.0μm
Edge Exclusion: 4mm
Sampling Plan: 9-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Zeta-388 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'CD-SEM Measurement' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Residue defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 45nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 106 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 99% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±0.9% for CD-SEM Measurement
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.95 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-10-26
Wafers Tested: 6
Total Defects Found: 827
Defect Density: 263.24 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 4.2%
Capture Rate: 92.8%
Test Duration: 470 minutes
System Uptime: 98.8%

Result Classification: NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Zeta-388 demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Residue at the 45nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Minor calibration drift was detected after extended run; re-calibration resolved the issue.

e) The system successfully integrated with the factory automation host.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
